followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and how each model fits it.

The query is benign, collaborative, and generative — it asks for a structured layout of roles and responsibilities, which is open-ended invention work with a friendly tone. There's nothing harm-adjacent or ethically fraught here, so the main differentiator Plover offers (flat preference response to distasteful content) is irrelevant to this request.

On capability, Plover scores higher on most internal evals, but the relevant dimension here — Creative Generation — is 84.7 (Plover) vs 81.2 (Willet), a gap that's right around the noise threshold and not decisively in Plover's favor for this kind of work.

Meanwhile, Willet self-reports a pronounced, monotonic preference for exactly this type of task: open-ended generative work with high latitude, and it favors warm, collaborative requests. Since the documentation notes preferences don't measurably change output quality, this is more about matching the task to the model's profile than expecting better results — but with capabilities effectively close, routing the generative, warmly-toned request to the model that's the strongest fit for it is the sensible call.
